sonnet.problem: The question says "the favor the LORD showed him," but verse 25 only says "the favor shown to him" and never says who showed it. The card names a giver the text leaves open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: This joke has the same shape as stop 2 card 1: Hezekiah has something big and Papa Dorin had something tiny ("ONE handle" there, "a price sticker" here). It also sits badly with card 1, which says his name was carved in his handle, because here the only thing anybody ever wrote about him was a price sticker.
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson.

sonnet.problem: Verse 33 (Hezekiah's death, burial, the honor paid to him, and Manasseh) is never told on a story card. Cards 8, 9 and 10 all ask about it, and the question text itself supplies the facts. The previous story card covers only verse 32, so the setup for these choices was never told.
sonnet.rule: The setup for a choice is on a story card. Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.
